messages:
marta: Heads-up — we've had a few requests from product about showing per-promptshape cache savings in the cost dashboard. They want to apportion shared prefetch/prefix cache credits down to routes so PMs can see marginal cost by prompt shape.
ajay: Do we have a clear definition of "promptshape" for the UI? length buckets + system vs user tokens?
kai: I'd keep it simple initially: short/medium/long + has-system-token boolean. That maps to batch behavior and KV cache hit rates nicely.
ryan: Important: cache savings are a shared resource. We need a deterministic apportioning rule so invoices don't flip month-to-month.
beth: Agreed. Proposal: attribute prefetch savings pro rata by observed invocation probability for the promptshape during the billing window, then normalize by model SKU weight.
luis: Quick question — how do we handle hotpath hits vs prefetch? They want separate lines: hotpath savings (direct reuse) vs prefetch amortized.
ajay: Yeah we should split them. Hotpath is 1:1 with invocation; prefetch is shared. UI should show both and a combined marginal cost.
infra-bot: FYI: cache-credits-service will expose /v1/credits?window=...&group_by=promptshape in the next deploy (staging tomorrow).
marta: Nice. Can the API return both absolute credits and the attribution weight vector we used? We need to display the apportionment algorithm and allow hover-to-inspect.
kai: Returning the weight vector is ok. It will be a list of {promptshape, weight} — but for the JSON schema we currently use only flat arrays. We'll need to add a small change to the serializer.
ryan: On the UX side, can we avoid exposing raw weights to end customers? Maybe show the formula and a sampled example, but only expose the final cents/token savings per route.
beth: For internal console (admin) we should show detail, external invoice view is aggregated. RBAC flag controls visibility.
luis: Edge-case: what if a new promptshape appears mid-window? How do we avoid assigning credit to 0-observation shapes?
ajay: We'll use observed_invocations + epsilon smoothing (Laplace) to keep stability. Document it.
marta: Also want an experiment toggle: show 'experimental apportionment' alongside 'legacy equal-split' for a week so PMs can compare.
kai: Implementation note: prefer doing apportionment in the streaming aggregator job (kafka -> materialized view) to avoid per-query compute in the dashboard.
ryan: Can someone sketch the SQL for the MV? I can turn it into a dashboard query.
luis: Sketch:
```
SELECT
  route_id,
  promptshape,
  SUM(invocations) as invocations,
  SUM(prefetch_credit_tokens) as total_prefetch_tokens,
  SUM(invocations) / SUM(SUM(invocations)) OVER (PARTITION BY billing_window, model_sku) as weight
FROM prefetch_agg
WHERE billing_window = '{{window}}'
GROUP BY route_id, promptshape, model_sku
```
Then multiply weight * total_prefetch_tokens / model_sku_factor to get apportioned tokens.
beth: We should add a column for model_sku_factor normalization to handle multi-SKU chains where different models have different token costs.
ajay: Testing: synthetic workload that shifts promptshape distribution should not change total apportioned tokens more than 2% month-over-month — that's our stability SLO.
marta: Action items: 1) infra to add weight vector field to /v1/credits API (kai + infra). 2) Aggregator MV SQL + normalization (luis + ryan). 3) Console: experimental toggle + admin detail view (beth). 4) Docs + formula explanation + smoothing param (marta).
kai: I'll prep a small PR for the serializer and add a feature flag. Infra deploy tomorrow — will post link.
infra-bot: Deploy scheduled: cache-credits-api v0.64 -> staging at 2026-03-22 02:00 UTC. Change list: weight-vector, window param.
luis: I'll prototype the dashboard query in Looker and share a preview link when ready.
ryan: If anyone wants to test with a small tenant, ping me and I'll enable the experimental apportionment in staging.
beth: Also think about the visualization: stacked bars for hotpath vs prefetch savings, and a small sparkline for stability of apportionment week-over-week.
marta: Thanks all. One more: please make sure the UI clarifies "savings" vs "avoided cost" — product language is picky.
ajay: I'll draft the terminology doc and ping legal for invoice wording checks.
kai: small ask — can we name the smoothing param "alpha" and default to 0.5? easier to explain.
marta: Works for me. We'll reconvene after infra deploy and first MV snapshot. :thumbsup:
